Class Parsley

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.Parsley
public final class Parsley extends Object
Composes Stages into a runnable application.

Run broker-less against TopologyTestDriver with testTopology(), or on a cluster with streams(Properties).

Stages connect through ordinary topics. One stage's sink is another's source, and the connecting topic is a causal channel like any other, stamped on write and gated on read. It must exist before the application starts.

A topic may be a sink of several stages, but a source of only one.

    • named

      public static Parsley named(String applicationId, Stage... stages)
      Composes stages into an application under the given id.

      Keep the id stable across deployments. It names the state stores, their changelog topics and the tick topics, and streams(Properties) pins application.id to it.

      Parameters:
      applicationId - the application id, matching [a-zA-Z0-9._-]+
      stages - the stages, in declaration order
      Returns:
      the composed application
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the application id is null or does not match, if no stages are given, if two stages share a name, or if a topic is a source of more than one stage

    • testTopology

      public org.apache.kafka.streams.Topology testTopology()
      Builds a broker-less topology for TopologyTestDriver.

      Topic identity is synthesized, each topic has one partition, and there is nothing to seed against or truncate. Every call assembles a new Topology, because Kafka Streams consumes one on construction.

      Use it with the test driver only. Against a real cluster it captures no consumer positions and resolves no real topic identity, and fails closed at the first delivered record.

      Returns:
      a fresh topology

    • streams

      public CausalStreams streams(Properties props)
      Assembles the cluster runtime, not yet started.

      Forces processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2 and isolation.level=read_committed, and sets application.id to the composition's. Resolves topic identity through an Admin client built from the same properties, which the returned handle closes with itself.

      Set listeners on the returned handle, then CausalStreams.start() it.

      Parameters:
      props - the Kafka Streams configuration
      Returns:
      the runtime handle, not yet started
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the properties name a processing.guarantee other than exactly_once_v2, or an application.id other than the composition's
